title: Establishing credibility for implicit FEA of intraocular lens haptics under capsular contraction: dual-model, tri-mechanism assessment under ASME V&V 40
device: Foldable intraocular lens (IOL) with open-loop haptics intended for capsular bag fixation

models.name: Model D3
models.what_it_computes: A detailed 3D implicit finite element model of the optic–haptic assembly in contact with a deforming capsular bag that computes haptic stresses, capsule–haptic contact pressures, and optic tilt/decentration under prescribed capsular contraction.

models.name: Model RB
models.what_it_computes: A reduced-order implicit finite element ring–beam model that represents the capsule as a contracting ring and the haptics as curved beams connected to a rigid optic, computing global stiffness, peak beam stress, and optic kinematics under contraction loads.

mechanisms.name: Uniform equatorial contracture
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Circumferential shrinkage of the equator elevates haptic loads, risking optic tilt and haptic overstress during postoperative capsular bag fibrosis.

mechanisms.name: Sectoral fibrosis with directional shrinkage
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Localized contraction in a capsular sector drives asymmetric contact and tilt/decentration, a clinically observed failure mode leading to visual disturbances.

mechanisms.name: Anterior capsulorhexis phimosis
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Contraction of the anterior capsule rim increases anterior edge tension and can impinge on haptic crowns, altering load paths and inducing malposition.

deviation.detail: All credibility factors and overall model risk are rated on a 0–4 Credibility Index (0=None, 1=Low, 2=Moderate, 3=High, 4=Very High).

sections: Question of interest: Does the proposed haptic geometry maintain mechanical performance under postoperative capsular contraction without increasing risk of optic tilt, decentration, or haptic overstress?

Context of use (COU): The two implicit FEA models will be used to predict haptic stress, capsule–haptic contact pressure, and optic tilt/decentration for three capsular contraction mechanisms across the intended power range. These predictions constitute the primary evidence to down-select a haptic design variant and to justify omission of additional benchtop capsular bag simulant tests for the screened mechanisms. The COU is limited to foldable IOLs implanted in-the-bag, with posterior capsule intact, and contraction magnitudes within the postoperative range reported clinically.

Model risk under ASME V&V 40: Credibility Index = 3/4. Rationale: Model influence is high because simulation outputs are the decisive evidence for design selection in the COU. Decision consequence is moderate because incorrect conclusions could lead to postoperative malposition manageable by clinical intervention (e.g., capsulotomy or IOL exchange) with low likelihood of permanent serious harm.
Device and mechanisms of capsular contraction
Computational models: geometry, contact, materials, and boundary conditions (implicit FEA)
Credibility factor: Model form — governing equations, contact formulations, and representation of capsule–haptic interaction for each mechanism and model
Credibility factor: Model inputs — geometric tolerances, material properties, and boundary condition magnitudes for each mechanism and model
Credibility factor: Numerical code verification — benchmark and patch-style verifications establishing correct implementation for each model
Credibility factor: Numerical solver error — mesh and load-step convergence, contact stabilization assessment for each mechanism and model

Credibility factor: Output comparison — comparison of predicted tilt, decentration, and stress trends against independent physical or literature data under analogous loading for each mechanism and model
Credibility factor: Relevance of the quantities of interest — alignment of QOIs (peak haptic von Mises stress, peak equatorial contact pressure, optic tilt angle, and decentration) to the COU
Credibility factor: Use error — summary of user workflow controls and default settings intended to reduce misuse in routine design studies
